summary.websitePass: HomeV2, MenuPanels, DeathScreen, HUD, Obelisk routes, README, launch docs, and manifest were reviewed. The strongest pattern is not missing depth; it is feature density competing across Command Center, Codex, What's New, Rules, Run History, DeathScreen, and measurement/status copy. The plan prioritizes consolidation, truthful account/trust surfaces, real visual media, first-run comprehension, and extraction work that keeps future sessions cheaper.

candidates.title: Front-Door Clarity Spine
candidates.why: The default front door is strong, but it now carries a DEPLOY dropdown, Command Center, Intel Ticker, mutation banner, measurement status, tabs, Codex subsections, and many modal panels. New players need one spine: deploy, learn what matters next, inspect optional depth only when asked. Consolidating repeated Rules/Codex/What's New/Command Center entry points into a progressive Journey Map will make the game feel more premium and less like a stack of successful prior sessions.
candidates.recipe: Create a `src/utils/playerJourney.js` model that classifies visitors as first-run, early-run, returning, mastery, or account-curious. Use it in `HomeV2.jsx` to show one primary next action, one secondary learning/action card, and a collapsed More panel that groups Codex, Rules, What's New, Controls, and Support without duplicating labels across the first viewport.
candidates.evidence: `src/components/HomeV2.jsx` renders Command Center buttons at lines around the COMMAND CENTER block, a Codex tab with ASSETS/ARSENAL/MOST WANTED/RULES/WHAT'S NEW, separate top-level tabs, Intel Ticker, weekly mutation, and a measurement status banner. `src/components/MenuPanels.jsx` also has Rules and What's New panels, creating repeated information paths.

L1.recipe: Hide the measurement/status banner from normal visitors and collapse Command Center by default until the player has at least one completed run or opens it manually.

L2.recipe: Add `playerJourney.js`; use it to drive a single next-action card plus a grouped More drawer; merge duplicate Rules/What's New entry points behind the same modal sources.

L3.recipe: Add journey-aware layout snapshots and Playwright visual checks for first-run, returning, supporter, and account-curious states across desktop/mobile.

candidates.title: Obelisk Verify + Guest Migration Receipts
candidates.why: Session 100 correctly made `/login` and `/auth/callback` explicit without gating play, but callback still depends on `/api/obelisk-verify`. This is the next trust boundary: account copy should not imply durable recovery until a server-side verification path exists. A guest-to-account receipt can preserve the free-play posture while letting signed-in players recover callsign, supporter state, progress, and leaderboard ownership.
candidates.recipe: Implement a Cloudflare Pages Function or Worker endpoint for `/api/obelisk-verify` that verifies the returned Obelisk token server-side, returns a redacted identity receipt, and stores a local `cod-obelisk-identity` receipt only after verification. Add tests for success, missing token, failed verify, and guest-play route preservation.
candidates.evidence: `src/obelisk-callback.js` defaults to `/api/obelisk-verify`, `src/ObeliskCallback.jsx` stores the result on success, and `context/LATEST_HANDOFF.compact.md` says no backend verify endpoint exists. `src/obeliskRoutes.test.js` proves guest play is the required default for `/`, `/daily`, and unknown paths.

L1.recipe: Add a visible callback error state that clearly says account recovery is not complete when `/api/obelisk-verify` is unavailable.

L2.recipe: Add the verify endpoint, callback tests, and route preservation tests without adding a gameplay gate.

L3.recipe: Add guest-to-account migration receipts for callsign, supporter flag, career stats, and leaderboard ownership, with rollback-safe local-first behavior.

candidates.title: Launch Screenshot Truth Pack
candidates.why: The launch media gate proves placeholder exports exist, but the public manifest still advertises stylized SVG stills instead of captured gameplay. For a browser game, real action screenshots sell trust faster than feature lists. Replacing placeholder store imagery with verified gameplay captures is the highest-return visual credibility upgrade now that the asset pipeline exists.
candidates.recipe: Use Playwright on the strict `53173` dev server to capture desktop combat, boss, builds/debrief, leaderboard, and mobile control screenshots. Update `public/manifest.json` screenshot paths to production PNG captures, update `assets/visual-assets.json` statuses to production-ready, and keep generated launch art as supplemental promotional media.
candidates.evidence: `public/manifest.json` points all five screenshots at `/launch-assets/*.svg`; `docs/LAUNCH_EXECUTION.md` says real gameplay captures are still a follow-up; Session 98 SIL names gameplay screenshot capture as the next visual credibility step.

L1.recipe: Capture one desktop combat PNG and one mobile controls PNG, add manifest/provenance entries, and leave SVG fallbacks intact.

L2.recipe: Replace all five manifest screenshots with verified gameplay PNGs and update launch docs/status.

L3.recipe: Add `npm run launch:screenshots` using Playwright screenshots plus pixel checks so future captures are reproducible.

candidates.title: First-Run Control Rite
candidates.why: The game already has input calibration, pointer sweep evidence, controller labels, and an onboarding list, but the player experiences them as advice rather than a ritual. Turn the first aim sweep into a tiny in-world readiness ceremony that awards a local badge and unlocks confidence before the first serious run. This makes launch QA infrastructure double as player delight.
candidates.recipe: Promote the existing input calibration nudge into an optional `AIM CHECK` pre-run micro-screen for first-run/debug states. Drive four target pips around the player, save the calibration record, show controller/mouse coverage, and grant a local `Controls Verified` chip in HomeV2 and Run History.
candidates.evidence: `HomeV2.jsx` already calls `buildInputCalibrationNudge`; `HUD.jsx` and App input debug paths expose calibration data; tests include pointer 360 coverage. No current surface makes the calibration feel like a completed player achievement.

L1.recipe: Add a HomeV2 `AIM CHECK` action that opens a short instruction/state panel using existing calibration summary.

L2.recipe: Add the four-direction micro-screen, save proof, and surface `Controls Verified` on the front door.

L3.recipe: Add controller-specific drift/dead-zone hints and a shareable local QA receipt for founder launch checks.

candidates.title: DeathScreen Next-Run Drill Bridge
candidates.why: The debrief has strong local intelligence: build grade, replay proof, ghost death readout, choke warning, weapon mismatch, run arc, rivalry ladder, and share tools. The missing step is a one-tap drill that converts the diagnosis into the next run configuration. This keeps the zero-token Run Brain decision intact while making the AI-like loop feel more alive.
candidates.recipe: Create `src/utils/drillDirector.js` that maps run coach outputs, ghost death readout, choke wave, top killer, and weapon mismatch into one `nextDrill` object. Render a single `RUN THE FIX` button on DeathScreen that launches the same seed/mode with a recommended difficulty/loadout or opens Most Wanted/Loadouts when a run is not appropriate.
candidates.evidence: `DeathScreen.jsx` currently renders many post-run cards and has buttons for Play Again, Replay Seed, Share Run, Leaderboard, and Menu. It does not produce one synthesized corrective action from the existing coach signals.

L1.recipe: Add a deterministic `nextDrill` line under Run Coach and route it to existing Replay Seed or Menu actions.

L2.recipe: Add `drillDirector.js`, tests, DeathScreen CTA wiring, and local Studio event tracking for drill shown/accepted/completed.

L3.recipe: Close the loop by comparing the next run to the drill objective and showing `DRILL WORKED` or `TRY AGAIN` feedback.

candidates.title: Visitor-Safe Status Copy
candidates.why: The front door currently shows operational measurement details such as `PostHog key missing`. That is useful to agents and developers, but it is not visitor-facing product information and can make a polished public game feel unfinished. Move operational status into a debug/admin path and keep the normal home screen focused on player value.
candidates.recipe: Gate the HomeV2 measurement-status banner behind `?debug=ops`, localStorage `cod-debug-ops=1`, or a dev build check. Replace normal visitor copy with no banner unless there is a player-actionable local/offline state, and add a small test proving `PostHog key missing` is absent in the default launch surface.
candidates.evidence: `src/components/HomeV2.jsx` renders a `MEASUREMENT STATUS` banner when analytics are disabled or local event sync has pending/failed state. `docs/LAUNCH_EXECUTION.md` explicitly says PostHog and Sentry are post-launch follow-up items, not launch gates.

L1.recipe: Hide the banner unless `import.meta.env.DEV` is true.

L2.recipe: Gate behind `?debug=ops` and add a launch-surface regression assertion.

L3.recipe: Add a compact Ops Panel under debug mode that groups analytics, event sync, service worker cache, and build identity.

candidates.title: Death/Submit Runtime Extraction
candidates.why: `src/App.jsx` is now nearly 4,800 lines even after many successful extractions. The death, submit, event digest, replay proof, rivalry, mission, and share-card transitions are high-change surfaces because every new coaching/trust idea touches them. Extracting this orchestration into pure helpers reduces future token spend and lowers the chance of editing the main game loop for UI/trust work.
candidates.recipe: Create `src/systems/deathFlow.js` and move death summary assembly, mission/career side-effect planning, trace evidence packaging, and post-run prop composition into tested pure builders. Keep App.jsx as the owner of refs/state setters, but shrink the death path to calling builders and applying returned effects.
candidates.evidence: `src/App.jsx` sample is 267,674 bytes / 4,785 lines. `docs/APP_EXTRACTION_ROADMAP.md`, `context/RISK_REGISTER.md`, and multiple closeout briefs identify death-slice extraction as the next architecture target.

L1.recipe: Extract only DeathScreen prop composition into `deathFlow.js` with snapshot tests.

L2.recipe: Extract prop composition plus score-submit event planning and mission/career summary builders.

L3.recipe: Build a headless death-flow harness that runs synthetic run endings and verifies all local events, replay proof receipts, and debrief props.

candidates.title: HUD Collision Budget
candidates.why: The HUD has become feature-rich: wave/timer, score, kill feed, mission progress, build archetype, ghost pack, weekly rival, heat, pace, experiment, weapon toolbar, synergy, and mobile controls all compete for fixed canvas edges. A visual collision budget will protect the elite feel on mobile and small desktops before another chip is added.
candidates.recipe: Add a HUD layout allocator that reserves top-center, top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-center, and bottom-right slots with priorities and viewport thresholds. Use Playwright screenshots to assert no key HUD regions overlap on desktop, mobile landscape, and narrow emulation while running a seeded busy state.
candidates.evidence: `HUD.jsx` uses many absolute-positioned blocks with dynamic top offsets for vsScore/topGhosts/weeklyRival and left chips for streak/experiment/pace. There is no centralized slot allocator or overlap test.

L1.recipe: Add a debug-only HUD bounding-box overlay and document current slot occupancy.

L2.recipe: Introduce priority slots for the dynamic top/left chips and add screenshot checks for overlap-free states.

L3.recipe: Let HUD density presets drive the allocator so Min/Standard/Tactical modes choose different chip priorities automatically.

candidates.title: Persistent Ghost Path Opponents
candidates.why: The HUD can show Ghost Pack targets and the debrief can replay the player's death path, but players still do not race a visible opponent during the run. Showing a faint leaderboard ghost path or checkpoint ribbon turns asynchronous competition into a living arcade rivalry without multiplayer infrastructure. This is a high-immersion feature that reuses the replay/trust groundwork already paid for.
candidates.recipe: Extend `loadTopGhosts()` data into compact path checkpoints when available, render a low-alpha ghost ribbon or next checkpoint marker in `drawGame.js`, and expose a setting to disable it. If leaderboard rows lack path data, show checkpoint deltas only and record the schema gap in trust docs.
candidates.evidence: `HUD.jsx` renders a Ghost Pack strip from `topGhosts`; `DeathScreen.jsx` renders local ghost path replay from `sessionStorage`; no live in-run ghost body/path is drawn from leaderboard data.

L1.recipe: Show a simple `RIVAL PACE` checkpoint marker using available score/wave deltas, no path rendering.

L2.recipe: Render compact ghost path checkpoints when stored locally or fetched, with opt-out setting and draw tests.

L3.recipe: Persist trusted ghost traces server-side and let players choose rival, daily champion, or personal-best ghost before deploy.

candidates.title: Local Balance Lab
candidates.why: The game already collects local Studio events and run history, but balance insight is spread across Run History, trust recommendations, mission streaks, and debrief cards. A zero-token Balance Lab can act like a local designer: identify over-deadly waves, ignored weapons, high-abandon modes, and upgrade traps, then produce tuning candidates for future audits. This improves AI/intelligence without violating the zero-token Run Brain decision.
candidates.recipe: Add `src/utils/balanceLab.js` that consumes run history, rivalry history, mission progress, and Studio events to emit ranked local insights. Surface a debug/admin Balance Lab panel under `?debug=ops` and include its top findings in audit/startup helpers without sending player data to an external model.
candidates.evidence: `HomeV2.jsx` loads `loadStudioGameEvents()` and summarizes them; `RunHistoryPanel` already computes trust recommendations and weekly contracts. No single local analyzer turns those records into design/balance recommendations.

L1.recipe: Add a pure analyzer for top death waves, top killer enemy, abandoned modes, and underused weapons with tests.

L2.recipe: Add the Balance Lab panel plus startup/audit-readable JSON export.

L3.recipe: Add counterfactual recommendations, such as difficulty curve nudges and loadout-specific tutorial prompts, validated against recent local runs.

candidates.title: Release Security Header Gate
candidates.why: The project has Cloudflare headers and many launch checks, but account routes, external Obelisk script loading, service worker caching, Supabase functions, and canonical redirects make release security a moving target. A single release gate should verify CSP/header posture, service worker version sanity, public-safe docs, and account-route expectations before launch or SPARKED status.
candidates.recipe: Extend `scripts/launch-readiness.mjs` or add `scripts/security-release-gate.mjs` to fetch local/prod headers, verify CSP includes only intentional origins, assert `/login` and `/auth/callback` are explicit surfaces, check service worker cache version freshness, and confirm `npm audit --json` is clean.
candidates.evidence: `cloudflare/` contains source-controlled security header config; `public/sw.js` is cache-bearing; `src/ObeliskLogin.jsx` loads `https://obeliskgate.com/auth-client.js`; package overrides recently fixed five vulnerabilities. These deserve one combined regression gate.

L1.recipe: Add header and route assertions to `launch-readiness.mjs --json`.

L2.recipe: Add a standalone release security gate and wire it into `npm run launch:verify`.

L3.recipe: Add live production comparison plus an allowlisted CSP diff that fails on unreviewed external origins.

candidates.title: Legacy Home Retirement Gate
candidates.why: HomeV2 is the default, but legacy MenuScreen remains reachable and duplicates What's New, Command Center, and several menu/panel concepts. Keeping a fallback is valid until evidence says otherwise, yet it increases maintenance and content drift risk. A retirement gate gives the repo a clear path to delete or freeze the legacy surface without guessing.
candidates.recipe: Add a `legacyHomeRetirement` checklist script/doc that requires HomeV2 launch smoke, mobile/desktop screenshot parity, no unique v1-only flows, and an explicit decision entry. If the gate passes, remove `?home=v1`; if it fails, freeze v1 content and mark it fallback-only.
candidates.evidence: `context/DECISIONS.md` says legacy MenuScreen remains lazy fallback until data gate. `src/components/MenuScreen.jsx` still has its own What's New and Command Center sections while HomeV2 is default.

L1.recipe: Document the remaining unique legacy MenuScreen behaviors and mark v1 fallback-only in code comments.

L2.recipe: Add a retirement checklist script/doc and update tests to assert HomeV2 covers all launch-critical paths.

L3.recipe: Remove the v1 fallback, delete duplicate code, and verify bundle/test/launch-surface changes.

skipped.reason: Rejected on verification: `context/DECISIONS.md` locks Run Brain as zero-token/local-first. The current signals are sufficient for deterministic coaching, and adding paid/token AI would increase privacy and cost without clear quality gain.

Rejected on verification: Session 100 explicitly restored guest-first gameplay and route tests require `/`, `/daily`, and unknown paths to render the game. Account work should add recovery/trust, not block free play.

Rejected on verification: current 2D canvas gameplay has extensive replay/input/trust coverage. The safer visual path is real screenshots, pseudo-3D primitives, and authored sprite assets before any gameplay renderer migration.

Deferred: the verified surface already has seven modes, many panels, and deep post-run systems. Current leverage is clarity, feedback closure, and trust rather than another mode competing for attention.

executionLog.notes: Gated the HomeV2 measurement-status banner behind `?debug=ops` / `cod-debug-ops=1` so ordinary visitors no longer see operational copy such as `PostHog key missing`. Added focused HomeV2 tests proving default visitor hiding and debug-surface visibility. Validation: `npx vitest run src/components/HomeV2.test.jsx` 7/7 and game medium gate passed.

Added `scripts/security-release-gate.mjs`, `security:release`, and `security:release:audit`, then wired the audit-backed gate into `launch:verify`. The gate checks required security headers, Content Security Policy directives, Obelisk route boundaries, service-worker cache versioning, lockfile presence, and `npm audit --json` when requested. Fixed CSP to allow the explicit Obelisk script/connect origin in both `public/_headers` and the Cloudflare security-header worker. Validation: static gate passed, audit-backed gate passed with 0 vulnerabilities, focused Obelisk route tests passed, and game medium gate passed.

Added `functions/api/obelisk-verify.js` as a Cloudflare Pages Function proxy that verifies returned Obelisk session tokens only when `OBELISK_VERIFY_URL` is configured, optionally uses `OBELISK_VERIFY_SECRET`, returns redacted identity receipts, and reports an honest `verify-not-configured` state otherwise. Updated the SPA callback helper to preserve backend failure reasons/details, documented the server env vars, and extended the security release gate to require the endpoint while preserving guest-first routes. Validation: endpoint/callback/route tests passed 8/8, audit-backed security gate passed with 0 vulnerabilities, and game medium gate passed.

Added `docs/LEGACY_HOME_RETIREMENT.md` and `scripts/legacy-home-retirement-gate.mjs`, exposed as `npm run home:retirement-gate`. The gate confirms HomeV2 is default, legacy `MenuScreen` remains lazy fallback-only, shared MenuPanels cover deep systems, launch smoke covers the default path, and the decision log still requires a data gate before removal. Validation: retirement gate passed, `npm run launch:smoke` passed, and game medium gate passed.

Added `src/utils/playerJourney.js` plus tests, stopped auto-expanding Command Center for returning players, and wired a compact HomeV2 Journey card that keeps DEPLOY primary while surfacing one next best secondary action such as Aim Check, Daily, Upgrades, Missions, Challenge, or Codex. Validation: playerJourney/HomeV2 focused tests passed 12/12, `npm run launch:smoke` passed, and game medium gate passed.

Promoted Aim Check from a passive nudge into a HomeV2 verification panel with four directional targets, a local controls-verified receipt using the existing input calibration record format, and a diagnostics escape hatch. The Journey card and quick chip now route to this single verification surface, and the front door updates to `AIM CHECK VERIFIED` after completion. Validation: HomeV2/inputCalibration/playerJourney focused tests passed 17/17, `npm run launch:smoke` passed, and game medium gate passed.

Added `src/utils/drillDirector.js` plus tests to synthesize one corrective next-run drill from choke warnings, Enemy Lab, weapon mismatch, ghost death readouts, Run Intelligence, or debrief actions. DeathScreen now renders a `NEXT DRILL` card with a `RUN THE FIX` / `PLAY THE FIX` CTA that reuses replay/play-again paths and records shown/accepted Studio events. Validation: drillDirector/runCoach/launch focused tests passed 21/21, `npm run lint` passed, and game medium gate passed.

Added zero-token `src/utils/balanceLab.js` plus tests to rank local design signals from run history, Studio events, career recent-death patterns, and weapon usage. HomeV2 now shows the top Balance Lab finding only in `?debug=ops` / ops-debug mode, keeping normal visitors on player-facing copy. Validation: balanceLab/HomeV2 focused tests passed 13/13, `npm run lint` passed, and game medium gate passed.

Added `src/utils/hudLayout.js` plus tests and wired a debug-only HUD slot overlay behind `?debug=hud` / `cod-debug-hud=1`. The overlay maps top-left, top-center, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-center, and bottom-right budget zones without affecting normal gameplay rendering. Validation: hudLayout/useGameLoop focused tests passed 7/7, `npm run lint` passed, and game medium gate passed.

Added `src/utils/rivalPace.js` plus tests and wired a compact in-run `RIVAL PACE` HUD chip that picks the nearest score target from weekly rival and Ghost Pack data. It uses the existing center-stack spacing budget so challenge score, ghost pack, weekly rival, and rival pace banners do not occupy the same top-center slot. Validation: rivalPace/hudLayout focused tests passed 6/6, `npm run lint` passed, and game medium gate passed.

Added `scripts/capture-launch-screenshots.mjs`, `npm run launch:screenshots`, `docs/LAUNCH_SCREENSHOT_TRUTH_PACK.md`, and two verified Chromium gameplay captures under `public/launch-captures/`. Updated launch docs, asset provenance, and the media gate so authored SVG stills remain fallback/promotional media while literal screenshot requests use verified capture PNGs. Validation: screenshot capture command exited cleanly, `npm run launch:media-check` passed, `npm run lint` passed, static security gate passed, and game medium gate passed.

Added `src/systems/deathFlow.js` plus tests and moved DeathScreen prop composition out of the App render branch into the pure `buildDeathScreenProps()` helper. App still owns refs/state/handlers, but the high-change debrief prop mapping is now isolated for future death-submit extraction work. Validation: deathFlow/App launch focused tests passed 3/3, `npm run lint` passed, and game medium gate passed.
